study: CarbonGate v2: forecast-based deferral of GitOps deployments on the GB grid (trace-driven simulation)
registered_before: Bulk download of the 12-month carbon-intensity record and before any policy simulation. Only a single 13-day probe (November 2025) was inspected to confirm the API response format.

data.source: NESO Carbon Intensity API, national /intensity/{from}/{to} (forecast and actual, 30-minute slots) and regional /regional/intensity/{from}/{to} (forecast only)
data.calibration_window: 2025-11 (used only to fix the static threshold and the capacity cap)

workload: SIMULATED non-homogeneous Poisson deployment arrivals (weekday 09:00-18:00 Europe/London rate 4 per hour, otherwise 0.25 per hour), 10% urgent deployments that bypass the gate, per-deployment energy from a declared CPU/memory power model (assumed coefficients).
hypothesis_H1: Forecast-based deferral (CarbonGate-F) with a 4 h maximum-delay SLA, deciding on the NESO forecast field only and scored on the NESO actual field, reduces deployment-attributed operational emissions relative to immediate deployment by at least 5% on held-out months, with zero SLA violations.
primary_endpoint: Relative emission reduction R = 1 - sum_i E_i * I_actual(policy start_i) / sum_i E_i * I_actual(immediate start_i), computed per held-out month (seed-averaged over 5 seeds); summary = mean over 11 held-out months with a two-sided 95% t confidence interval (n = 11 months).
baseline: Immediate deployment (standard GitOps reconciliation, no carbon gate).
comparators: static threshold gate (threshold = calibration-month median forecast, released at the SLA deadline)
oracle deferral (perfect foresight of actual intensity within the SLA window; upper bound)

decision_rule.SUPPORTED: lower 95% CI bound of mean R > 0.05 AND SLA violation count = 0 in the primary configuration
decision_rule.REFUTED: upper 95% CI bound of mean R < 0.05 OR SLA violation count > 0 in the primary configuration

falsification_rule: H1 is refuted if the upper 95% CI bound of the mean held-out reduction is below 5%, or if any deployment in the primary configuration starts later than its 4 h deadline.
secondary_H2: Replication of the v1 claim: mean R of CarbonGate-F (4 h) >= 0.23. SUPPORTED if the lower 95% CI bound > 0.23, REFUTED if the upper bound < 0.23, otherwise INCONCLUSIVE.
planned_ablations: forecast source (NESO forecast, day-ahead persistence, NESO forecast + Gaussian noise, actual)
forecaster outages and timeouts with fail-open, fail-closed, and cached-persistence fallbacks
x100 load with a per-slot capacity cap
untestable: marginal-emission reductions (no marginal data for GB)
